label: Pillar Two / GloBE Compliance Workflow
description: Run a group's global minimum tax compliance cycle through four gates: the scoping determination under Directive (EU) 2022/2523, the election and safe-harbour ledger (de minimis, initial-phase, the internationally agreed safe harbours and the side-by-side treatment), the top-up computation approach, and the top-up tax information-return filing plan with its 15/18-month deadlines. Complements the Pillar Two exposure assessment — this one decides what the group elects and files, and by when.

claudeKnowledge.description: Council Directive (EU) 2022/2523 (Union Pillar Two instrument: scope Art. 2, IIR Arts. 5-10, QDMTT Art. 11, UTPR Arts. 12-14, ETR Art. 26, top-up tax Art. 27, SBIE Art. 28, de minimis Art. 30, safe harbours Art. 32, filing Art. 44, elections Art. 45, transitional SBIE rates Art. 48, initial-phase exclusion Art. 49, 18-month transition-year filing Art. 51, transposition Art. 56); OECD/G20 GloBE Model Rules and Commentary; Inclusive Framework Administrative Guidance and the agreed safe-harbour package (transitional CbCR safe harbour, QDMTT safe harbour, transitional UTPR safe harbour, side-by-side and ultimate-parent relief); GloBE Information Return; national implementing acts and local registration/notification deadlines

guidedInputs.label: Ultimate parent entity jurisdiction
guidedInputs.description: Where is the UPE located? This decides which charging rule reaches the group, which implementing act governs, and whether the side-by-side question arises at all — the workflow cannot start without it.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Sweden; Germany; United States; Japan

guidedInputs.label: Fiscal year being worked (and the first in-scope year, if different)
guidedInputs.description: Almost every downstream rule is keyed to the fiscal year: the transition-year treatment, the year-specific substance carve-out rate, the safe-harbour transition period and the filing deadline.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. FY ending 31 December 2026; first in-scope year was the FY beginning 1 January 2024

guidedInputs.label: Which gates should this run cover?
guidedInputs.description: The four gates run in order and each depends on the one before. Leave all selected for a full cycle; narrow it when you are re-running a single gate.

options.label: Gate 1 — Scoping determination (threshold, entity map, charging provisions)
Gate 2 — Elections, exclusions and safe harbours
Gate 3 — Top-up computation approach and data sequence
Gate 4 — Information-return and notification filing plan

guidedInputs.label: Group footprint and figures
guidedInputs.description: Consolidated revenue for the relevant preceding fiscal years, number and location of constituent entities, joint ventures, and any jurisdiction you expect to sit below a 15% effective tax rate.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Consolidated revenue EUR 1.9bn and EUR 2.1bn in the two preceding fiscal years. About 35 constituent entities across Sweden, Germany, Ireland, Switzerland, Luxembourg, the UK and the US, plus a 50/50 manufacturing JV in Poland. Ireland and Luxembourg look borderline on ETR; the Swiss cantonal rate is below the headline.

guidedInputs.label: Host jurisdictions operating a domestic top-up tax
guidedInputs.description: List every jurisdiction where the group has entities and a domestic minimum top-up tax is in force or expected. This is tested separately from any group-level relief and is never switched off by it.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. Ireland, Switzerland and the Netherlands all operate a domestic top-up tax; we are unsure about the UAE free-zone entity and have not checked Singapore.

guidedInputs.label: Which data can the group actually produce today?
guidedInputs.description: Anything left unselected becomes a data-readiness flag rather than an assumption — that is how the gaps get into the plan.

options.label: Qualified financial statements per constituent entity
Deferred tax recast at the lower of the domestic rate and 15%
Eligible tangible-asset carrying values by jurisdiction
Controlling-interest / ownership map for every constituent entity
Prior-year top-up tax information return or equivalent

guidedInputs.label: Elections already made, prior positions and open questions
guidedInputs.description: A five-year election made in an earlier year still binds this one. Note anything already elected, any relief already relied on, and the questions you actually want answered.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. We took the de minimis exclusion for two small jurisdictions last year and relied on the transitional CbCR safe harbour everywhere else. No SBIE election has been made. Open questions: does the initial-phase exclusion still apply after we opened a seventh jurisdiction, and who has to notify in Germany if the Swedish UPE files centrally?

exampleInput: We are the group tax function of a Swedish-headquartered industrial group (consolidated revenue about EUR 2.1bn, roughly 35 constituent entities across Sweden, Germany, Ireland, Switzerland, Luxembourg, the UK and the US, plus a 50/50 JV in Poland). Our first in-scope year was the fiscal year beginning 1 January 2024 and we are now planning the cycle for the fiscal year ending 31 December 2026. We do not want another exposure model — we have one. What we need is the compliance workflow: (1) confirm the scoping determination and which charging provision reaches each part of the group, including what the side-by-side position means for our US sub-group and whether it touches the Irish and Swiss domestic top-up taxes at all; (2) build the election ledger — which reliefs we should test, which elections bind for five years versus one, who makes them and by when; (3) set out the computation approach for the jurisdictions that are not switched off after the reliefs, with the year-specific substance carve-out rates; and (4) give us a dated filing plan covering the return, the local notifications and the internal close, working back from the deadline. Known weakness: our consolidation cannot split covered taxes or deferred tax by jurisdiction, and nobody owns the eligible payroll and tangible-asset extract.

modelTier.notes: The election ledger and the charging-provision ordering interact across jurisdictions and terms; a smaller model reliably produces the list but collapses the group-level relief and the host-jurisdiction domestic top-up tax into one answer.
